task.description: Step 1 of WF-03 for ISS-0421: diagnose exactly how much of the issue's original 3-part scope (unbounded serial-sweep latency, platform-wide SPOF, default restart intensity) is still open now that REQ-219 (supervision layering + Pollers restart-intensity override) and ISS-0451 (PollersBreaker circuit breaker) have both merged, and route to the correct next step rather than assuming the issue's original framing still holds in full.

result.summary:
Verified against the CURRENT merged code (not the issue's own prose) that 2 of ISS-0421's 3 original concerns are now fully, structurally resolved, and 1 remains genuinely open and unaddressed by either REQ-219 or ISS-0451. Findings:

(1) CONCERN 3 -- default restart intensity -- FULLY RESOLVED. `lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers.ex` sets `Supervisor.init(children, strategy: :one_for_one, max_restarts: 5, max_seconds: 60)` (REQ-219), and its own moduledoc records the override and rationale verbatim under a '## Restart intensity override -- DELIBERATE, not the OTP default' heading, satisfying AC5's moduledoc requirement. AC2's test intent ('a repeatedly-crashing Poller does not bring down Letflow.Repo or the rest of the app') is satisfied and then some: `test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs` has a full `describe "AC4: crash-loop isolation"` block (test: 'a Poller crash-looping past Pollers' own restart intensity restarts only Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers') asserting `Letflow.Repo`'s pid is unchanged across an induced crash-loop -- and `test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker_test.exs` additionally covers the PERSISTENT-fault case ISS-0451 exists for ('top-level Supervisor, Repo, and Http survive a persistent crash-loop, and the breaker trips to :open'), which is a strictly stronger property than ISS-0421's original AC2 asked for (ISS-0421 only worried about a single crash-loop event; ISS-0451 also closes the persistent/repeating case). No further work needed here.

(2) CONCERN 2 -- platform-wide SPOF -- FULLY RESOLVED, confirmed by reading `lib/letflow/application.ex`'s current top-level shape directly. The 20-child flat list is gone; `start/2`'s children list is now `[Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure, Supervisor.child_spec(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary), Letflow.Supervisor.PollersBreaker, Letflow.Supervisor.Http]` under `strategy: :one_for_one`. Pollers is structurally isolated in its own sibling supervisor (REQ-219), and ISS-0451 additionally gives Pollers' own child spec `restart: :temporary` so the top-level Supervisor can NEVER auto-restart it (verified in `pollers_breaker.ex`'s and `application.ex`'s own comments, both citing a live probe: 10 repeated kill/start_child cycles left a `max_restarts: 1` top-level supervisor alive throughout). `PollersBreaker` (a GenServer, not a Supervisor child of Pollers) is the sole restart authority for Pollers via `Supervisor.start_child/2`, with an exponential-backoff open/half-open/closed state machine (1s/5s/30s/2m/5m cap) so a PERSISTENT Poller fault degrades to 'Pollers stopped, not crash-looping' rather than ever reaching the top level. `Letflow.Repo` and Bandit (`Letflow.Supervisor.Http`) are two supervisor-boundaries away from Pollers and are never touched by any Poller fault, transient or persistent. Top-level intensity was also raised from OTP-default 3/5 to 5/5, justified as pure headroom for unrelated Infrastructure/Http/PollersBreaker coincidences, not as compensation for any Pollers-attributable consumption (which is now proven exactly 0). This is a strictly stronger resolution than ISS-0421's original AC2/AC5 asked for. No further work needed here.

(3) CONCERN 1 -- unbounded serial-sweep latency -- STILL FULLY OPEN, confirmed by reading the current `handle_info(:tick, state)` in `lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex` (lines 160-193) and its 6 sweep helper functions (`maybe_refresh_active_instances/1`, `maybe_run_retention_sweep/2`, `maybe_run_alert_detection/3`, `maybe_run_ordering_cycle/1`, `maybe_run_ordering_sweeper/1`, `maybe_run_ordering_metrics/1`, plus the top-level `Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1` loop) verbatim. Every one of the 7 sweeps still does `Enum.each(schemas, fn schema_name -> with_admission(schema_name, :op, fn -> ... end) end)` -- fully serial, `Enum.each`, no `Task.async_stream` or any other concurrency primitive anywhere in this file. `tenant_schemas/0` (via `fetch_tenant_schemas/0`) is still called exactly once per tick and its result (`schemas`) is threaded through all 7 sweeps unchanged -- AC4's 'single query per tick' property is intact and would need to be preserved by any fix. Neither REQ-219 nor ISS-0451 touched this loop or its helpers at all -- REQ-219 only added a test-only forced-crash guard clause as `handle_info`'s FIRST expression (a 3-line double-gated `if`/`raise`, orthogonal to the sweep logic), and ISS-0451 touched no file under `lib/letflow/scheduler/` at all. REQ-218's admission-control wiring (`with_admission/3`, a `:global` semaphore acquire/release per schema/operation call) bounds how many CONCURRENT operations may run platform-wide once concurrency exists, but does not itself introduce or bound any concurrency -- the calls it wraps are still issued one at a time, so it does not touch the latency-scaling problem ISS-0421's concern 1 describes. This confirms the codebase's own requirements.yaml record (REQ-219's own 'SEQUENCING NOTE FOR ISS-0421' and 'NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT' paragraphs, docs/requirements.yaml ~lines 13052-13065) already anticipated exactly this outcome: 'ISS-0421's own internal Poller fix (bounding the 7 serial per-tenant sweeps, e.g. via Task.async_stream) -- separate, narrower, sequenced to land after this requirement.' REQ-219's own decision 3 (Pollers max_restarts:5/max_seconds:60) is explicitly the settled input ISS-0421's fix must build on, not re-decide.

SCOPING/ROUTING DECISION: This is now a NARROWER issue than originally filed -- concerns 2 and 3 are closed (and, for concern 3, closed more strongly than ISS-0421 itself asked for, via ISS-0451's persistent-fault handling). Concern 1 remains a real, non-trivial design decision requiring CODE-DESIGNER, not a mechanical fix: (a) choice of concurrency bound for `Task.async_stream(schemas, fun, max_concurrency: N)` across (potentially) 7 call sites, one per sweep; (b) DBConnection pool-budget math against `pool_size: 10` -- N must be chosen (and justified with arithmetic, matching this codebase's own established bar, e.g. REQ-219/ISS-0451's precedent of quoting live-probe numbers) so that peak concurrent DBConnection checkouts across whichever sweeps may run concurrently within one tick (and, per REQ-218, interacting with `Letflow.Admission`'s existing `:global` semaphore) never exceeds what pool_size 10 can serve -- ISS-0224's own SandboxPool precedent is the cited hazard class to avoid repeating; (c) preserving the single `tenant_schemas/0` query per tick (`schemas` must still be computed once and threaded to all 7 sweeps, async or not); (d) deciding whether all 7 sweeps get independent bounded concurrency or share one bound/one Task.Supervisor, and whether a slow/erroring tenant in one sweep should affect that tenant's OTHER sweeps in the same tick or only that one sweep -- none of this is prescribed by ISS-0421's own text ('Suggested direction, NOT prescribed (CODE-DESIGNER decides)') and genuinely needs a design pass, not an ad-hoc implementation.

Recommend: do NOT close/fold ISS-0421 as fully resolved. Instead, narrow its remaining scope to concern 1 only (concerns 2 and 3 can be noted as resolved-by-REQ-219/ISS-0451 in the eventual close comment) and route to CODE-DESIGNER for a fix design covering (a)-(d) above, affected file `lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex` only (no supervision-tree changes needed -- REQ-219/ISS-0451 already own that ground). No re-diagnosis needed by CODE-DESIGNER; this summary is the full root-cause/scope statement.

next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER: design a fix for ISS-0421's remaining, narrowed scope (concern 1 only -- unbounded per-tenant serial-sweep latency in lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex's handle_info(:tick, state) and its 7 sweep call sites), per result.summary above. Concerns 2 (platform-wide SPOF) and 3 (default restart intensity) are already fully resolved by REQ-219 + ISS-0451 and require no further design work; CODE-DESIGNER should not re-touch lib/letflow/supervisor/ or lib/letflow/application.ex for this issue.
